title: Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Amendment (Veterans’ Allied Health Care) Bill 2026
short_title: Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Amendment (Veterans’ Allied Health Care) Bill 2026

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would protect specified allied health treatment and compensation entitlements for veterans and dependants from spending caps and reviews triggered by expenditure thresholds.
It would prohibit required gap payments and restrictions imposed solely or substantially because aggregate treatment costs approach or exceed a set amount, while preserving clinical controls.
The protections would apply from the day after Royal Assent to treatment and compensation entitlements arising before or after commencement, without reopening earlier final amounts.
changes: An inclusive definition of allied health professionals would allow regulations to add professions without removing those expressly covered.
The Treatment Principles could not use spending thresholds as the sole or substantial reason to interrupt allied health care.
Compensation pathways would be protected from aggregate caps, while a new provision would allow reimbursement to be limited to actual treatment costs.
Regulations could extend protection to additional statutory treatment and compensation pathways.
summary.affected: Eligible veterans, dependants, allied health practitioners and the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Commission are affected.
